claims.claim: **Syncope** = brief, sudden loss of consciousness and postural tone with spontaneous recovery. About 15% of children have an episode by the end of adolescence.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **An arrhythmia should be considered in every child with syncope**, even though syncope in children is mostly vasovagal. Cause and investigation are best guided by a thorough history.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reflex (vasovagal) syncope** has a clear precipitant — tiredness, hunger, heat, dehydration, emotion.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Orthostatic hypotension:** within 2–3 minutes of standing, systolic falls over 20 mmHg or diastolic over 10 mmHg. Causes include hypovolaemia, anaemia, electrolyte disturbance, menorrhagia, medications.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **POTS:** chronic, daily orthostatic intolerance **plus** a heart-rate rise on standing (within 5–10 minutes) of more than 40 bpm — or more than 30 bpm without postural hypotension.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cardiac causes:** brady/tachyarrhythmia, long QT, Brugada, CPVT, conduction disease such as WPW, and structural disease (congenital heart disease, cardiomyopathy, myocarditis).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mimics:** seizure, migraine, hypoglycaemia, toxins (carbon monoxide, clonidine), functional disorder, narcolepsy.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unconsciousness:** usually seconds in autonomic and cardiogenic syncope; **with seizures, longer than a few seconds and up to minutes.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Incontinence** is absent in autonomic and cardiogenic syncope and may be present in seizures; **confusion on waking** is absent in both syncope types and **marked for 20–30 minutes after a seizure.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tonic-clonic movements** are occasional and brief in either syncope type, particularly with prolonged unconsciousness (syncopal seizure); **frequent in seizures.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Measure orthostatic heart rate and BP**, and do a complete cardiac and neurological examination.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **ECG in every child at least once** — may be skipped only if done before with no new concern.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **BGL** when seen soon after the event, **FBE** when anaemia is suspected, and consider a pregnancy test.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Frequent or problematic vasovagal or orthostatic syncope:** avoid triggers, **increase fluid and salt intake**, and recognise prodromal symptoms early.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected cardiac syncope on history, examination or ECG: refer urgently to a paediatrician or cardiologist.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer** recurrent vasovagal/orthostatic syncope unresponsive to non-drug measures (paediatrician or cardiologist), and seizure-like presentations (paediatrician or neurologist).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer** if persistently symptomatic, or with clustering of syncope with cardiac features.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** once the most likely cause is identified and follow-up is arranged.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Syncope' (Last updated November 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Syncope/, retrieved 2026-09-23
